markingScheme:
Apply the power rule to each term **(1 mark)**
$\tfrac{d}{dx}(3x^2) = 6x$ **(1 mark)**
$\tfrac{d}{dx}(-4x) = -4$ **(1 mark)**
$\tfrac{d}{dx}(7) = 0$ **(1 mark)**
Final answer $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 6x - 4$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.explanation: The derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives, so we differentiate $3x^2$, $-4x$, and $7$ separately.
The derivative of any constant is $0$, so $\tfrac{d}{dx}(7) = 0$.
